--- Respondent
 For Applicant : Mr. Sudeep Agrawal, Advocate

For Respondent/State : Ms. Pragya Shrivastava, Dy. Ga.
 Hon'ble Shri Justice Arvind Kumar Verma
 Order on Board
09/01/2025
1.

This is first bail application filed under Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 for grant of regular bail to applicant, who has been arrested in connection with Crime No.24/2024,
registered at PS - Mahila Thana, Ambikapur, District Surguja, Chhattisgarh, for commission of offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 323 & 506 (part-II) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 5(L) & 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Case of the prosecution in brief is that present applicant has established physical relationship with minor victim on the pretext of marriage and also assaulter her by means of hands and fist, due to which, she suffered grievous injuries.
Based upon report, aforementioned crime/offence has been registered against the applicant and he has been arrested on 23.06.2024.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in this case,
he has not committed any offence as alleged against him.
There is love affair between the applicant and victim and they performed marriage as per rituals prevalent in Gond community.
Learned Counsel further submits that victim has examined before the trial Court and not supported the case case of prosecution.
There is no any other criminal antecedents against the applicant.

Applicant is in Ravi Kumar vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190563800/
1 jail since 23.06.2024, conclusion of trial may take some time, hence, applicant may be released on bail.
4.

entities.text: Ravi Kumar vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned State Counsel opposes the bail application and submits that there is specific allegation against the applicant of committing forceful sexual intercourse with the minor victim aged about 17 years and 10 months, hence, he is not entitled for grant of regular bail.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
6.
Pursuant to order of this Court, prosecutrix/victim is appeared before this Court by virtual mode from the concerned DLSA.
She submits that she is having no objection in granting bail to the applicant.

7. Considering facts of the case, nature of allegations, submission of learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant and victim have performed the marriage, victim has turned hostile and has not supported the case case of prosecution, further considering that there is no any other criminal antecedent against the applicant, charge-sheet has already been filed, applicant is in jail since 23.06.2024, conclusion of trial may take some time, without commenting anything on merits of the case, I am inclined to allow this bail application.
8.
Accordingly, bail application is allowed.

It is directed that applicant shall be released on regular bail, on his furnishing a bail bond in sum of Rs.10,000/- with one surety in like sum to satisfaction of concerned Court on the conditions that- a) Applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such fact to the Court.

b) Applicant shall not act in any manner which will be prejudicial to fair and expeditious trial, and c) Applicant shall appear before trial Court on each and every date given to him by the said Court till disposal of the trial.
Certified copy as per rules.

Sd/-
(Arvind Kumar Verma) Judge J.
